## 9. Install-Writes Non-Exposure (v1 invariant)

`Clearerrorhistory` (selector `02 01`) and `Clearservicehistory` (selector
`02 02`) are classified `INSTALL_WRITE` (§4) and are subject to the following
normative v1 invariant:

> **`02 01` and `02 02` MUST NOT be exposed on any public surface in v1.**
> This includes, without exception, MCP tools, GraphQL mutations, portal UI
> affordances (including hidden / feature-flagged DOM), and Home Assistant
> services.

Enforcement:

- `M2a_GATEWAY_MCP` acceptance includes a negative test asserting no MCP tool
  exists for these selectors.
- `M2b_GATEWAY_GRAPHQL` acceptance includes a schema introspection diff
  asserting no mutation exists for these selectors.
- `M3_PORTAL` acceptance includes a DOM audit scanning for any element
  referencing `clear`, `delete`, or `reset` keywords in the B503 pane.

Any future exposure of these selectors requires a **separate plan** and a new
doc-gate PR per `AGENTS.md §8.4`, including installer-mode authentication
design and isolated-hardware bench evidence.

SESSION_STATE_CONTRACT.reason: Preserve the existing session state contract contract obligation.
SESSION_STATE_CONTRACT.value:
five stable states: `Idle`, `Enabling`, `Active`, `Refreshing`, and `Disabled`.
`Refreshing` means an epoch refresh holds the ownership gate. The already
admitted triggering request remains pending; subsequent bus-facing live-monitor
operations are busy. Refresh success dispatches a triggering read exactly once
and returns `Active` only when that dispatch completes without a transport
disconnect; a disconnect follows the any-transport-disconnect transition below
and releases the owner. Refresh success may instead dispatch a triggering
current-owner disable exactly once after its frame reaches emission. A terminal
disconnect while that request still waits for poll-quiesce emits no disable,
returns `TRANSPORT_DOWN`, releases the owner, and retains fail-closed cleanup;
it is never retried on reconnect. Every emitted disable result is recorded and
returned exactly, but the result alone never establishes native session
settlement. Refresh failure releases the gate, enters internal `DISABLED`,
retains a Gateway cleanup obligation, and returns the exact Gateway-supplied
failure to that request; its public session observation is `Idle` with
`owned:false` and unavailable capability. `Disabled` is never reported with
`owned:true`.

DISABLED_PUBLIC_MAPPING.reason: Preserve the existing disabled public mapping contract obligation.
DISABLED_PUBLIC_MAPPING.value:
**Stable public `Disabled` mapping:** `Disabled` with `owned:false` represents
only an out-of-band administrative/configuration-disabled condition supplied
by Gateway. It is never the result of a current-owner live-monitor session
DISABLE action; every terminal outcome of that action presents public `Idle`
with `owned:false`, retains cleanup, and publishes `UNKNOWN`. A still-effective
out-of-band disabled condition takes precedence across Gateway restart and
continues to present `Disabled` with `owned:false`. Enable failure, the 30s idle
timeout, transport disconnect, and every other restart-derived internal cleanup
path may traverse `DISABLED`, but their stable public session observation is
`Idle` with `owned:false`. While a process-local cleanup obligation remains,
capability is `UNKNOWN` and Enable is unavailable; `Idle` does not make the
internal slot re-claimable. `Disabled` is never reported with `owned:true`.

REFRESHING_CLEANUP_CONTRACT.reason: Preserve the existing refreshing cleanup contract contract obligation.
REFRESHING_CLEANUP_CONTRACT.value:
When a locally token-owning consumer leaves a target or navigates away while
its session is `Refreshing`, it MUST queue that target/token disable without
invoking the busy operation. After successful refresh reaches `Active`, it
dispatches the queued disable unless a terminal disconnect occurs before frame
emission; that path emits no disable and returns exact `TRANSPORT_DOWN`. After
refresh failure releases ownership and presents `Idle`, it clears the browser
queued pair without a client disable while Gateway retains the process-local
cleanup obligation. If the triggering request was itself the current-owner
DISABLE, that admitted request is the only client dispatch. Its emitted native
outcome, or its pre-emission `TRANSPORT_DOWN`, is returned and recorded exactly,
while Gateway retains process-local fail-closed cleanup. The consumer clears
the queued pair without issuing a second disable.

ENABLING_CLEANUP_CONTRACT.reason: Preserve the existing enabling cleanup contract contract obligation.
ENABLING_CLEANUP_CONTRACT.value:
When a consumer leaves a target or navigates away while its locally initiated
enable is pending, it MUST register cleanup under the exact
`(targetAddress, localEnableAttemptID, presentationEpoch)` tuple. The consumer
allocates a fresh opaque `localEnableAttemptID` before dispatch and never reuses
it. Successful
completion of that same attempt supplies the issuer token and dispatches
exactly one target/token disable. Any other completion—including `ctx.Done`
before bus turnaround, ACK timeout, NAK, CRC mismatch, bus-arbitration timeout,
epoch-advance discard, transport disconnect, gateway restart, or any other
terminal failure—clears that registration without issuing a client disable
before any later enable is admitted. The registration MUST NOT transfer to a
later attempt or session. Gateway may separately emit the single defensive
native disable required by the §6.3 terminal-failure transition.

REFRESHING_UNKNOWN_STRIP_CONTRACT.reason: Preserve the existing refreshing unknown strip contract contract obligation.
REFRESHING_UNKNOWN_STRIP_CONTRACT.value:
During a held `Refreshing` epoch, the
session strip remains observable alongside temporarily `UNKNOWN` capability,
but it is status-only: only `vaillantCapabilities` and
`vaillantLiveMonitorSession` remain admitted so the client can observe
completion. No B503 card, general tabs, bus-facing reads, or actions are
admitted while Gateway reports `Refreshing`. If the triggering READ succeeds
and rebinds the same target and issuer token into `Active` with `owned:true`,
the bounded current-owner READ/DISABLE exception above resumes immediately
under `UNKNOWN`; it does not wait for `AVAILABLE` and does not extend to a
different target, token, or general `UNKNOWN` presentation.

ACTIVE_UNKNOWN_OWNER_CONTRACT.reason: Preserve the existing active unknown owner contract contract obligation.
ACTIVE_UNKNOWN_OWNER_CONTRACT.value:
After a successful Enable ACK, session is `Active` with `owned:true` while
capability remains `UNKNOWN` because settlement is unproven. The consumer that
still holds the exact current issuer token for that target may retain the
session strip and dispatch only current-owner READ or DISABLE. It MUST NOT
admit a second Enable, general B503 tabs, a new projection entry, or those
controls for another `UNKNOWN` target/session. Target switch, navigation away,
ownership loss, or departure from `Active` removes this exception and follows
the cleanup contract below.

REFRESH_SUCCESS_CONTINUATION.reason: Preserve the existing refresh success continuation contract obligation.
REFRESH_SUCCESS_CONTINUATION.value:
- On refresh success for a surviving authenticated current-owner handle, the
  old epoch-N key authorizes only that refresh. Gateway atomically installs the
  returned current `transport_key` for epoch N+1 with the same issuer token and
  target before returning to `Active`; every epoch-N completion is fenced. This
  is continuation, not reconstruction or auto-resume. The already-admitted
  triggering request remains pending during refresh; after successful rebind,
  Gateway dispatches that request's native operation exactly once using the
  rebound key and returns its exact outcome. A triggering READ retains the
  owner in `Active` only when its dispatch completes without transport
  disconnect; a disconnect releases the owner into `DISABLED`. A triggering
  current-owner DISABLE emits its disable exactly once after quiesce only when
  the frame reaches emission, records and returns the exact native outcome,
  releases the owner, and remains in internal `DISABLED`. A terminal disconnect
  before emission instead emits no disable, returns exact `TRANSPORT_DOWN`,
  releases the owner, retains fail-closed cleanup, and is not retried on
  reconnect.
  ACK and NAK do not establish settlement: Gateway retains process-local
  cleanup, publishes `UNKNOWN`, and admits no Enable. ENABLE is never a refresh
  trigger. This dispatch consumes the request's only retry budget.

REFRESH_FAILURE_CAPABILITY_PRECEDENCE.reason: Preserve the existing refresh failure capability precedence contract obligation.
REFRESH_FAILURE_CAPABILITY_PRECEDENCE.value:
- On refresh failure, return the exact Gateway result—including
  `TRANSPORT_DOWN` or `UNKNOWN`—to the triggering caller. While the resulting
  cleanup obligation remains, public capability is `UNKNOWN`; the exact caller
  result MUST NOT be collapsed into `SESSION_BUSY`.

REFRESH_OWNER_REBINDING.reason: Preserve the existing refresh owner rebinding contract obligation.
REFRESH_OWNER_REBINDING.value:
On an `ACTIVE` epoch advance from N to N+1, the old `session_key` authorizes
only the one bounded refresh attempt. A successful refresh returns the current
`transport_key` for epoch N+1. Gateway MUST atomically replace the owner key
with `(transport_key[N+1], same issuer_token)` while retaining the same target,
then dispatch the admitted triggering operation exactly once. Completions and
control requests still bound to epoch N are stale and MUST NOT satisfy, disable,
extend, or mutate the rebound session. If refresh fails, no rebound key is
installed; Gateway releases client ownership, retains a fresh Gateway-owned
process-local cleanup obligation in internal `DISABLED`, presents public
session `Idle` with `owned:false`, publishes capability `UNKNOWN`,
and admits no Enable while native settlement remains unproven.

NO_AUTO_RESUME_RECONSTRUCTION.reason: Preserve the existing no auto resume reconstruction contract obligation.
NO_AUTO_RESUME_RECONSTRUCTION.value:
- Gateway MUST NOT reconstruct or auto-resume a session after restart, a lost
  owner handle, or an absent/invalid current issuer token. The surviving
  authenticated current-owner refresh path in §7.3 is the only continuation
  allowed across a non-terminal epoch advance.

REFRESHING_DISCONNECT_FENCE.reason: Preserve the existing refreshing disconnect fence contract obligation.
REFRESHING_DISCONNECT_FENCE.value:
- A terminal transport disconnect follows §7.4: it releases any held owner and
  does not enter `Refreshing` on reconnect. An `Idle` target with no owner or
  cleanup obligation stays `Idle` through disconnect/reconnect and requires a
  new explicit client Enable.
- If cleanup/session settlement is unproven, the transport layer MUST NOT
  publish the new epoch as B503-usable or admit Enable. Reconnect emits no
  automatic B503 enable or disable. Gateway preserves the process-local target,
  attempt, and prior epoch only as evidence/cleanup state, publishes `UNKNOWN`,
  and waits for a future accepted settlement contract.

DISCONNECT_CLEANUP_OBLIGATION.reason: Preserve the existing disconnect cleanup obligation contract obligation.
DISCONNECT_CLEANUP_OBLIGATION.value:
- An `ENABLING` disconnect before enable-frame emission cancels the queued frame,
  returns exact `TRANSPORT_DOWN`, releases `liveMonitorMu`, clears the attempt,
  retains no cleanup obligation, and returns directly to `IDLE`. Reconnect still
  requires a new explicit Enable and emits no automatic B503 write.
- After enable-frame emission, or from `ACTIVE` / `REFRESHING`, transport
  disconnect transitions the FSM to `DISABLED` and releases `liveMonitorMu`.
  If an Enable may have reached the wire or settlement is otherwise unproven, Gateway retains
  `(targetAddress, gatewayCleanupAttemptID, priorTransportEpoch)` only as a
  process-local cleanup obligation across transport reconnect. It carries no
  issuer token, owner authority, session continuation, or operation eligibility
  and cannot authorize an automatic reconnect write.

OWNER_CONDITIONAL_MUTEX_SCOPE.reason: Preserve the existing owner conditional mutex scope contract obligation.
OWNER_CONDITIONAL_MUTEX_SCOPE.value:
Only release of `liveMonitorMu` is owner-conditional (§6.3 "Lock lifecycle"):
it occurs only when an owner is held at the moment the event fires. Cleanup
obligations and their native outcomes remain effective after owner release,
including defensive cleanup while the FSM is already `DISABLED`; `IDLE` or
`DISABLED` makes the event a no-op only with respect to mutex release.

DISCONNECT_CLEANUP_MUTEX_INDEPENDENCE.reason: Preserve the existing disconnect cleanup mutex independence contract obligation.
DISCONNECT_CLEANUP_MUTEX_INDEPENDENCE.value:
- If the FSM was already `IDLE` or `DISABLED` at transport-disconnect time,
  disconnect is a no-op with respect to the mutex; no release is attempted. A
  pre-existing cleanup obligation remains across that disconnect.
- If the FSM was already `IDLE` or `DISABLED` at Gateway-restart time, restart
  is likewise a no-op with respect to the mutex. It still destroys every
  process-local cleanup attempt identity and enforces the per-target `UNKNOWN`
  fence; no prior attempt identity survives process restart.

CONFIRMED_CLEANUP_DEFINITION.reason: Preserve the existing confirmed cleanup definition contract obligation.
CONFIRMED_CLEANUP_DEFINITION.value:
An ACK or NAK is an exact native outcome, not proof that the device session
stopped or was never created. After any emitted Enable, Gateway may use one
bounded defensive disable during the same admitted lifecycle and records its
outcome, but no current 0.7 outcome makes the session slot re-claimable. Gateway
retains fail-closed cleanup, publishes capability `UNKNOWN`, and denies Enable
until a separately evidenced native settlement observation exists. Current
public evidence defines no such observation; its evidence and recovery contract
are deferred to [issue #525](https://github.com/Project-Helianthus/helianthus-docs-ebus/issues/525).

UNCONFIRMED_CLEANUP_OBLIGATION.reason: Preserve the existing unconfirmed cleanup obligation contract obligation.
UNCONFIRMED_CLEANUP_OBLIGATION.value:
- Every native disable used for explicit, idle-timeout, refreshed, or defensive
  cleanup records its exact ACK, NAK, timeout, CRC, arbitration, disconnect, or
  other outcome. No such outcome alone clears the obligation or proves native
  session settlement. Gateway retains the target plus a fresh Gateway-owned
  `gatewayCleanupAttemptID` and attempted transport epoch as process-local,
  operation-ineligible cleanup state, publishes `UNKNOWN`, admits no Enable,
  and performs no same-epoch or automatic reconnect/restart recovery.

GATEWAY_CLEANUP_ATTEMPT_ID.reason: Preserve the existing gateway cleanup attempt id contract obligation.
GATEWAY_CLEANUP_ATTEMPT_ID.value:
- Gateway allocates `gatewayCleanupAttemptID` when the cleanup obligation is
  created and never reuses it. This opaque ID is internal to Gateway; it is not
  the browser-local `localEnableAttemptID`, is not supplied by a caller, and
  confers no owner or operation authority.

CONFIRMED_CLEANUP_DIAGRAM.reason: Preserve the existing confirmed cleanup diagram contract obligation.
CONFIRMED_CLEANUP_DIAGRAM.value: DISABLED --> DISABLED: native outcome recorded; settlement remains unproven

EXPLICIT_DISABLE_PRE_EMISSION_DISCONNECT.reason: Preserve the existing explicit disable pre emission disconnect transition contract obligation.
EXPLICIT_DISABLE_PRE_EMISSION_DISCONNECT.value: | `ACTIVE` | current-owner session DISABLE action; transport disconnect before disable-frame emission | `DISABLED` | emit no disable frame, record and return exact `TRANSPORT_DOWN`, release the owner, retain the existing `(targetAddress, gatewayCleanupAttemptID, priorTransportEpoch)` as process-local cleanup, present public `Idle` with `owned:false`, publish `UNKNOWN`, admit no Enable, and perform no reconnect retry |

EXPLICIT_DISABLE_CONFIRMED_TRANSITION.reason: Preserve the existing explicit disable confirmed transition contract obligation.
EXPLICIT_DISABLE_CONFIRMED_TRANSITION.value: | `ACTIVE` | current-owner session DISABLE action; any terminal native outcome after disable-frame emission | `DISABLED` | the disable frame was emitted exactly once after quiesce; record and return its exact outcome, release the owner, retain `(targetAddress, fresh gatewayCleanupAttemptID, currentTransportEpoch)` as process-local cleanup, present public `Idle` with `owned:false`, publish `UNKNOWN`, and admit no Enable; this session action never produces public `Disabled`, and its outcome does not prove settlement |

RESTART_TRANSITION.reason: Preserve the existing restart transition contract obligation.
RESTART_TRANSITION.value: | any | gateway restart | `DISABLED` | release any owner and destroy every caller handle and process-local attempt identity; reconstruct no session, emit no automatic B503 enable or disable, and publish `UNKNOWN` for each qualified target; a still-effective out-of-band administrative/configuration-disabled condition presents public `Disabled` with `owned:false`, otherwise the restart-derived state presents public `Idle` with `owned:false`; admit no Enable under the current 0.7 contract |

RESTART_RELEASE_CONTRACT.reason: Preserve the existing restart release contract contract obligation.
RESTART_RELEASE_CONTRACT.value:
- On Gateway restart, Gateway transitions the FSM to `DISABLED` and, if an
  owner was held, releases `liveMonitorMu`. No session or cleanup tuple persists
  across restart. Because Gateway can no longer distinguish its pre-restart
  session from a session owned by another bus client, it emits no automatic
  B503 enable or disable. Each qualified target starts with live-monitor
  capability `UNKNOWN`, and Enable remains unavailable under the current 0.7
  contract.

RESTART_CLEANUP_FENCE.reason: Preserve the existing restart cleanup fence contract obligation.
RESTART_CLEANUP_FENCE.value:
- After every Gateway process restart, enumerate the finite registry-qualified
  B503 targets, set each target's live-monitor capability to `UNKNOWN`, admit no
  Enable, and emit no automatic B503 enable or disable. The Portal and GraphQL
  v1 surfaces expose no recovery control. Current 0.7 defines no ACK/NAK-based
  maintenance action that restores availability; later evidence and any changed
  recovery contract belong to deferred issue #525.

IDLE_TIMEOUT_ACK_CONTRACT.reason: Preserve the existing idle timeout ack contract contract obligation.
IDLE_TIMEOUT_ACK_CONTRACT.value:
- Gateway records the exact disable ACK, NAK, timeout, CRC, arbitration,
  disconnect, or other outcome, releases the owner, retains process-local
  cleanup, publishes `UNKNOWN`, and admits no Enable. No outcome alone returns
  the internal FSM to `IDLE` or preserves public `AVAILABLE` because native
  session settlement remains unproven. Idle auto-disable MUST NOT be reported as
  `NOT_SUPPORTED`, which is reserved for "device class does not implement
  B503" (§11).

IDLE_TIMEOUT_TRIGGER_CONTRACT.reason: Preserve the existing idle timeout trigger contract contract obligation.
IDLE_TIMEOUT_TRIGGER_CONTRACT.value:
- In `ACTIVE`, after 30 seconds without a successful read, Gateway emits a
  disable frame once after quiesce and transitions to `DISABLED`.

NORMALIZED_REFRESH_DISABLE_CONTRACT.reason: Preserve the existing normalized refresh disable contract contract obligation.
NORMALIZED_REFRESH_DISABLE_CONTRACT.value:
2. **Refresh once.** On epoch advance with a held session, Gateway transitions
   to `Refreshing` and makes exactly one refresh attempt. The already-admitted
   triggering READ or current-owner DISABLE remains pending and is dispatched
   exactly once only after successful rebind. READ returns Gateway to `Active`
   only when its dispatch completes without transport disconnect; a disconnect
   releases the owner under the `any` disconnect transition. DISABLE emits once
   only after its frame reaches emission and records and returns its exact native
   outcome. A disconnect before disable-frame emission emits no disable, returns
   exact `TRANSPORT_DOWN`, and is not retried. Both paths release ownership,
   retain fail-closed cleanup in internal `DISABLED`, publish `UNKNOWN`, and
   admit no Enable. Subsequent bus-facing live-monitor operations are
   `SESSION_BUSY` during refresh. Refresh failure likewise releases client
   ownership but retains Gateway cleanup, publishes `UNKNOWN`, and admits no
   Enable.

REFRESH_FAILURE_DIAGRAM.reason: Preserve the existing refresh failure diagram contract obligation.
REFRESH_FAILURE_DIAGRAM.value: REFRESHING --> DISABLED: refresh failure retains cleanup

REFRESH_READ_DIAGRAM.reason: Preserve the existing refresh read diagram contract obligation.
REFRESH_READ_DIAGRAM.value: REFRESHING --> ACTIVE: refresh succeeds; triggering READ completes without disconnect

REFRESH_DISABLE_DIAGRAM.reason: Preserve the existing refresh disable diagram contract obligation.
REFRESH_DISABLE_DIAGRAM.value: REFRESHING --> DISABLED: refresh succeeds; DISABLE emitted or pre-emission disconnect

UNCONFIRMED_CLEANUP_DIAGRAM.reason: Preserve the existing unconfirmed cleanup diagram contract obligation.
UNCONFIRMED_CLEANUP_DIAGRAM.value: DISABLED --> DISABLED: native outcome recorded; settlement remains unproven

REFRESH_READ_TRANSITION.reason: Preserve the existing refresh read transition contract obligation.
REFRESH_READ_TRANSITION.value: | `REFRESHING` | refresh succeeds for triggering READ; dispatched READ completes without transport disconnect | `ACTIVE` | atomically rebind the owner from epoch N to the returned current `transport_key` at N+1, retaining the same issuer token and target; fence every epoch-N completion; dispatch READ exactly once using the rebound key, return its outcome, and retain the owner; any transport disconnect instead follows the `any` disconnect row and releases the owner into `DISABLED` |

REFRESH_DISABLE_PRE_EMISSION_DISCONNECT_.reason: Preserve the existing refresh disable pre emission disconnect transition contract obligation.
REFRESH_DISABLE_PRE_EMISSION_DISCONNECT_.value: | `REFRESHING` | refresh succeeds for triggering current-owner DISABLE; transport disconnect before disable-frame emission | `DISABLED` | atomically rebind to the N+1 key, fence every epoch-N completion, emit no disable frame, record and return exact `TRANSPORT_DOWN`, release the owner, retain `(targetAddress, fresh gatewayCleanupAttemptID, transportEpoch[N+1])` as process-local cleanup, publish `UNKNOWN`, admit no Enable, and perform no reconnect retry |

REFRESH_DISABLE_TRANSITION.reason: Preserve the existing refresh disable transition contract obligation.
